title: Synoptic compatibility ledger and reconciliation playbook for fallback routing variants
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: establish and operationalize a single, synoptic compatibility ledger that captures tokenizer, context (KV/cache and max-length), and tooling parity for all fallback model variants used by smart routing policies. This ticket creates the reconciliation playbook, automation steps, and observability hooks so routing can safely fall back between variants without tokenizer/context regressions or silent tooling mismatches.

Background: our routing layer selects fallbacks by region, tier, and capacity. When a primary model is unavailable we currently rely on heuristics and a loosely-maintained compatibility matrix. This has caused intermittent user regressions (truncated tokens, mismatched structured output shapes, and subtle reranking score drifts) when fallbacks differ in tokenizer vocabulary or KV layout.

Scope:
- Define canonical compatibility keys and ledger schema (model_family, variant_hash, tokenizer_version, context_window, kv-layout-tag, tooling-profiles), stored in the synoptic registry.
- Implement reconciliation runbook to detect drift between primary and fallback variants and resolve: automated re-labeling, forced BQ scans, and escalation to model-onboarding.
- Audit all variants in circulation used by routing policies and mark status: green (compatible), amber (partial compatibility; requires mitigation), red (incompatible).
- Add pre-routing gating check and a safe fallback policy: if any tokenization or context mismatch risk is detected, route to alternative region/tier or use a strict compatibility variant.
- Add end-to-end tests, fuzz tokenization comparisons, and a CI gate for model onboarding that updates the ledger.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Ledger schema documented in Confluence and a PR with the initial ledger and migration script merged.
2) Automated reconciliation job added to infra (k8s CronJob) that produces daily delta reports and annotates variant status.
3) Routing layer pre-check calls ledger API and prevents an unsafe fallback path in 99.9% of observed mismatch cases (measured on staging traffic).
4) E2E regression test suite that asserts tokenizer parity for at least 95% of top-50 routing cohorts; failing cohorts create amber tickets.
5) Runbook and on-call playbook created and reviewed by Reliability and Applied ML.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New dashboard: Compatibility Ledger health (coverage, delta rate, amber/red counts).
- Alert: >1% new daily mismatches or any release that introduces a red-status fallback.
- Logs: tokenization mismatch diff samples retained for 30 days for triage.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement ledger schema + migration in a branch and run reconciliation locally against snapshot of variants.
2) Merge reconciliation job to staging, enable daily runs, and iterate on false-positive thresholds.
3) Wire routing pre-checks behind a feature flag in staging; run simulated traffic to validate no regression.
4) Gradual canary of pre-checks in production: 1%->10%->100% traffic over 7 days, monitor compatibility dashboard.
5) Flip feature flag and decommission older, incompatible fallback entries when mitigations complete.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Tight compatibility gating increases routing failures during outage, potentially causing higher latency if alternate region/tier selection is opted for. Mitigation: implement soft-fallback that serves with explicit quality stamp and logs for customer support.
- Ledger staleness if onboarding teams don't update model metadata. Mitigation: CI gate enforcement and PR templates for onboarding.
